description: Green-Gray Analysis: Assessing the Costs and Benefits of Green Infrastructure for Water Supply Systems is a web tool or resource listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by World Resources Institute. This downloadable guide gives stakeholders a way to value the costs and benefits of integrating green or natural infrastructure into water supply systems to improve performance. It builds on existing case studies of green and grey infrastructure analysis rooted in classic decision and public investment theory. Coverage: the United States, or as stated on the tool page. The toolkit lists hazards: Drought, Water Quality. Assets: Natural Areas and Wildlife, Water Infrastructure – Drinking Water, Water Infrastructure – General, Water Infrastructure – Wastewater. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
